steps.note: Start a new eRFX event for the RFQ bidding scenario.
Configure the event with an RFQ stage rather than the default auction stage.
Work on the RFQ stage before configuring its template and sheet.
Apply an available RFQ pricing template.
Add a line item so the RFQ bid sheet can be configured.
Commit a live bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite the vendor company whose two users are under test.
Publish the RFQ so Vendor A can bid.
Verify the event reached a published project page.
Submit User 1's bid for 100 from the vendor portal.

args.need: sign in as Vendor A's second user in a separate vendor session, open this live RFQ from the vendor event list, submit a bid of 98, and report whether Procol refuses it as an already placed team bid or treats it as a revision

steps.note: A second user account/session from the same vendor company is required to test the company-level duplicate-bid rule.

args.text: A bid has already been placed from your team

steps.note: Assert the specified refusal message when the second user's submission is rejected.
